ing: or 3 tbsp palm oil plus vegetable oil
st: Rub the chicken with [[2 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper, half the garlic and [[2 tbsp]] lemon juice. Marinate 20 minutes.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the chicken for 10 minutes.
Add the onions and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the remaining garlic, the chili and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the squash and okra and simmer 20 minutes until the squash is tender and the sauce is thick.
Check the chicken reached 165°F (74°C). Taste and adjust salt.
Serve with funge, rice or cassava.
Soak the dried fish in warm water for 1 hour. Drain, remove bones, and flake.
Heat the palm oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and chili and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until saucy.
Add the dried fish and [[1.5 cups]] water. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add the okra and spinach, cover, and cook 10 minutes.
Lay the fresh fish on top, sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt if needed, cover and cook 10 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Stir gently and serve with funge or rice.

ing: whole fish or fillets (such as tilapia or sea bass)
peeled and cut in chunks (or yuca)
st: Rub the fish with [[1 tsp]] salt, the pepper, minced garlic and juice of 1 lemon. Marinate for 20 minutes.
Boil the cassava and sweet potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] palm oil in a pot and cook the diced onion for 5 minutes. Add the beans and [[0.5 cup]] water and simmer 10 minutes.
Fry the plantain slices in [[3 tbsp]] vegetable oil for 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain.
Grill or broil the fish for 6 minutes per side until it reaches 145°F (63°C) and flakes easily.
Cook the sliced onion with [[2 tbsp]] palm oil and a splash of lemon juice for 5 minutes for the topping.
Arrange the fish on a platter with the beans, plantains, cassava and sweet potatoes.
Spoon the onions over the fish and serve with lemon slices.
Put the thawed cassava leaves in a pot with [[3 cups]] water. Bring to a boil.
Simmer for 40 minutes, until the leaves are very tender. Cassava leaves must be cooked well.
Drain half the water if there is a lot, but keep some for the sauce.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] palm oil in another pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and chili and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the ground peanuts and [[1 tsp]] salt, then add the cooked leaves.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Serve hot with rice or funge.

ing: dried beans (such as pinto or black-eyed peas)
st: Put the soaked beans and [[8 cups]] fresh water in a pot with the bay leaf.
Bring to a boil and boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer for 50 minutes until beans are nearly tender.
Heat the palm oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onions for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until jammy.
Stir the tomato mixture into the beans with [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until the beans are creamy and the sauce is thick.
Remove the bay leaf, mash a few beans on the side of the pot to thicken, and taste for salt.
Serve with rice, cassava or fried plantain.
Put [[1.5 cups]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water, the cinnamon stick and cloves in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes without stirring until a light syrup forms.
Add [[3 cups]] shredded coconut and cook on medium-low for 10 minutes, stirring, until the coconut is soft and the syrup is thick.
Remove the cinnamon stick and cloves and cool 10 minutes.
Beat the egg yolks in a bowl, then slowly stir in a few spoonfuls of the warm coconut to warm the yolks.
Pour the yolk mixture back into the pan.
Cook over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and the yolks are fully cooked. It should pull away from the pan.
Pour into a dish, sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] cinnamon, and cool before cutting or spooning.
